rules.claim: Named SubClassOf emits http://subclassof.
Bidirectional taxonomy also emits the reverse http://superclassof edge.
Some, only, min, and max object restrictions are supported.
A restriction in subclass position emits from the named superclass to its filler.
only_taxonomy suppresses restrictions but leaves other categories enabled.
Min/max cardinality numbers do not affect emitted edges.
Unqualified min/max restrictions use owl:Thing as filler.
Restrictions with complex fillers emit no edge.
Top-level union/intersection subclass shapes are ignored.
Only the first two encountered members of n-ary equivalence participate.
A named second equivalence expression is processed as a subclass pair.
A second-position intersection is expanded by operand.
A second-position union is expanded by operand.
A restriction in second equivalence position emits nothing and member orientation matters.
The subrole map looks up the prior value under the subproperty key.
No transitive subproperty closure is computed.
Sibling subroles can overwrite each other according to OWLAPI iteration.
Inverse mappings are bidirectional and the last visited collision wins.
Restriction edges expand through the historical inverse/subrole maps.
Domain/range projection requires named properties and classes.
Matching domain and range axioms form a property-local cross product.
OWLAPI classifies domain/range outside getRBoxAxioms, so the source's two collection sites make one effective pass; distinct annotated axioms can still preserve equal-edge multiplicity.
Anonymous domain/range expressions are ignored.
Named class assertions emit http://type.
Anonymous individuals and complex class assertions are ignored.
Named object-property assertions emit their direct triple.
Assertions receive no inverse/subrole expansion and data assertions emit nothing.
An inverse object-property assertion produces the pinned typed failure outcome.
include_literals scans classes from the closure but looks up annotations only in the root ontology, so an imported-only class annotation is not emitted.
Annotation inclusion is determined by the exact source allowlist of property IRIs.
String and RDF plain literals use their raw lexical form.
Other datatypes take the stripValue compatibility branch.
IRI-valued annotations take the bracket-stripping branch.
Unsupported properties and annotations on non-class subjects are not emitted.
Exact cardinality restrictions are ignored.
Object hasValue and self restrictions are ignored.
Data restrictions and data-property assertions are ignored.
Union/intersection quantified fillers are not normalized into accepted shapes.
Property chains and property characteristics produce no edge.
Unicode IRIs/literals are preserved without normalization.
Backslashes in non-plain stripValue values follow the source's removal behavior.
A one-level import contributes closure axioms and annotations.
A diamond import closure visits the shared ontology once as an ontology document.
A cyclic import closure loads and projects both documents.
The oracle's strict loader reports a missing import as a typed load failure before projection.
subRoles/inverseRoles persist when the same Scala projector instance is reused, including repeated, absent-map, and conflicting-map calls.
Category concatenation is subclass, equivalence, annotation, class assertion, object assertion, then domain/range; the output remains a bag.
